subtitle: Freeze the filtered signal at a defined instant while the ADC converts
takeaways: C_{H} window: droop sets the minimum, acquisition the max
Settle to ½ LSB: t_{acq} ≈ 0.69·(N+1)·τ ≤ t_{track}
Buffer both sides: follower, switch, C_{H}, follower

slides.title: Why sample and hold?
bullets: Defines the sampling instant t_{k} = k·T_{s}
Keeps the voltage constant while the ADC converts
Without S&H: |dV/dt|_{max}·t_{conv} < ½ LSB, e.g. 12 bit: f < 3.9 Hz
With S&H only the aperture time counts (nanoseconds)
Capstone: f_{s} = 5 Hz, 3-bit flash ADC, 0 to 4 V, LSB 0.5 V
slides.notes: Position in the chain: sensor, anti-aliasing low-pass, S&H, ADC. The 12-bit example (t_{conv} = 10 µs, 2 V amplitude) is worked in section Why Sample and Hold?. Even a flash converter needs a defined instant so the display does not flicker.

slides.title: Switch and hold capacitor
bullets: Clock high: switch closed, C_{H} follows V_{in} (track)
Clock low: switch open, C_{H} keeps its charge (hold)
Capstone clock: 5 Hz, duty cycle 10 %: track 20 ms, hold 180 ms
Errors: acquisition, aperture/jitter, pedestal, droop
slides.rule: Held value = V_{in} at the end of the track phase
slides.notes: Strictly this is a track-and-hold; the names are used interchangeably. R_{S} contains source resistance, switch R_{on} and the 1 kΩ that limits the op-amp charging current. The terms diagram is in section The Track-and-Hold Principle.

slides.title: Falstad: basic sample and hold

falstad.name: sh_basic
falstad.hint: Watch Vhold step once per 200 ms at the falling clock edge

observe: Output is a staircase, one step per sampling period
Held values about 5 mV below V_{in}: C_{H} lags a rising input
Change the duty cycle of the clock rail and watch the track window
slides.notes: V_{in} = 2 V + 1.5 V·sin(2π·0.5 Hz·t), R_{S} = 1 kΩ, C_{H} = 1 µF. Held values 2.094, 2.956, 3.452 V and so on. The lag is slope × τ = 4.7 V/s × 1 ms.

slides.title: Analog switches
bullets: nMOS switch: R_{on} grows as V_{in} approaches V_{G} − V_{th}
Transmission gate: nMOS + pMOS in parallel, almost constant R_{on}
Parts: CD4066, 74HC4066 (R_{on} ≈ 50 to 300 Ω), DG4xx; off leakage pA to nA
Falstad Analog Switch: closed above 2.5 V, R_{on} 20 Ω, R_{off} 10 GΩ
slides.notes: The Falstad switch has no charge injection and no leakage; we add them as discrete elements later. The 1 kΩ series resistor limits the charging current and keeps the op-amp stable with the large capacitive load.

slides.title: Acquisition: settle to ½ LSB
bullets: Charging: τ = (R_{S} + R_{on})·C_{H}, worst case a full-scale step
Design rule: t_{acq} ≤ t_{track}, upper limit for C_{H}
Capstone: τ = 1.02 ms, t_{acq} = 2.83 ms ≪ 20 ms

falstad.name: sh_acquisition
falstad.hint: 4 V step: 2.53 V after τ, 3.75 V (½ LSB below) after 2.83 ms

slides.notes: Use a time constant of a few percent of the track window; the rest is reserve for op-amp settling and tolerances. Derivation in section Designing the Hold Capacitor; Exercise 8.1.

slides.title: Droop: losing charge in hold
bullets: Leakage: open switch, dielectric, buffer bias current, PCB surface
Droop rate dV_{H}/dt = I_{leak}/C_{H}
t_{hold}: worst case the whole period T_{s} − t_{track}
Design rule gives the lower limit for C_{H}
slides.notes: Real leakage is pA to nA, so the lower limit is usually far away. The capstone allows ΔV_{max} = LSB/10 = 50 mV.

slides.title: Falstad: too small, right, too large

falstad.name: sh_capsize
falstad.hint: 3 V input, 50 nA leakage: compare 10 nF, 1 µF and 100 µF

observe: 10 nF: charges fully, but droops 3.00 V → 2.10 V per hold
1 µF: 3.00 V → 2.99 V, the right choice
100 µF: only 18 % per sample, 1.88 V after five samples
slides.notes: The leakage is exaggerated to make droop visible. A too large capacitor turns the S&H into a low-pass filter. Exercise 8.2.

slides.title: Design recipe: hold capacitor
steps: Track window t_{track} = D·T_{s} (capstone: 5 Hz, 10 %: 20 ms)
Upper limit: C_{H} ≤ t_{track}/((R_{S} + R_{on})·ln 2^{N+1}) = 7.1 µF
Lower limit: C_{H} ≥ I_{leak}·t_{hold}/ΔV_{max} = 36 nF (10 nA, 50 mV)
Pick the geometric middle: C_{H} = 1 µF, safety factor ≈ 7 each side
Use PP, PS film or C0G; never electrolytic capacitors
slides.notes: Capstone result: R_{S} = 1 kΩ, C_{H} = 1 µF film, t_{acq} = 2.8 ms, droop 1.8 mV at 10 nA. Electrolytics leak in the µA range. Dielectric absorption makes the held voltage creep back; film capacitors show little of it.

slides.section: Errors of a Real Sample and Hold
slides.title: Charge injection (pedestal)
bullets: Clock step couples through C_{gd} onto the hold node
C_{gd} = 10 pF, 5 V: −49.5 mV with 1 nF, −0.5 mV with 100 nF
Constant part can be calibrated, signal-dependent part cannot
Remedies: larger C_{H}, transmission gate, dummy switch

falstad.name: sh_pedestal
falstad.hint: 2 V input: Vhold_1n drops to 1.9505 V, Vhold_100n to 1.9995 V

slides.notes: Falstad models only the coupling capacitance, not the channel charge. Exercise 8.4.

slides.section: Errors of a Real Sample and Hold
slides.title: Feedthrough, aperture and jitter
bullets: Feedthrough: C_{ds} of the open switch couples V_{in} to C_{H}
Aperture delay: constant, only shifts the sampling instant
Aperture jitter: error ΔV = (dV/dt)·t_{j}; 12 bit, 1 MHz: t_{j} < 19 ps
Dielectric absorption: held voltage creeps back
slides.notes: Jitter is why fast converters need clean clocks. For the 5 Hz capstone a millisecond of jitter is harmless, see Exercise 8.6.

slides.title: Falstad: why both buffers?

falstad.name: sh_buffered
falstad.hint: Compare Vout_unbuf with the buffered output over one period

observe: Unbuffered (R_{i} 10 kΩ, R_{L} 100 kΩ): 2.425 V after track, 0.401 V at end
Buffered: 3.000 V during the whole period
Input buffer supplies the charge, output buffer draws none
slides.notes: The unbuffered circuit fails three ways: divider between source and load, slow charging, discharge through the load. Use a FET-input op-amp as output buffer; its bias current adds to I_{leak}. Exercise 8.3.

slides.title: Falstad: sampling a ramp

falstad.name: sh_staircase
falstad.hint: Triangle 0 to 4 V at 0.5 Hz: count the 0.8 V steps

observe: 0.8 V > 1 LSB (0.5 V): consecutive samples skip codes
Not an S&H error: the input is too fast for f_{s}
slides.notes: Clock rail: square, 5 Hz, 2.5 V amplitude, 2.5 V offset, duty cycle 0.1. Such fast signals must be removed by the anti-aliasing filter. Exercise 8.5.

slides.title: Practical hints
bullets: Rail-to-rail output for 0 to 4 V on 5 V; FET input for the output buffer
Guard ring around the hold node against surface leakage
Integrated S&H (LF398, AD783): only C_{H} external
SAR and sigma-delta ADCs sample internally: driver must settle in t_{acq}
slides.notes: The LF398 data sheet has acquisition time and droop curves versus C_{H}, a good illustration. Microcontroller SAR inputs sample with a few pF; the same t_{acq} = τ·ln 2^{N+1} calculation limits the source resistance.
